source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Face the client in good lighting, speak clearly at a normal volume and pace, and use written or other preferred communication methods when helpful.","B":"Face the client but substantially increase volume and exaggerate mouth movements because louder, exaggerated speech improves understanding with hearing loss.","C":"Speak from the client's better-hearing side while looking toward the chart because visual access to the speaker's face adds little when hearing is impaired.","D":"Direct most questions to a companion and let the companion relay answers because hearing loss makes direct client communication less reliable."}}
source_row.rationale: Communication should be adapted to the client's hearing needs. Option A is correct because facing the client in good lighting, speaking clearly without shouting, and using preferred written or other methods can improve communication. Option B is incorrect because shouting and exaggerated speech can distort communication. Option C removes visual access to the speaker's face. Option D unnecessarily redirects communication away from the competent client.
